title: add-traffic-curation-probe-scaling-and-staged-throttle-guard
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our existing canary probes surface regressions but noisy traffic and transient microbursts cause false positives and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces a traffic curation layer and probe-scaling levers that reduce noise while preserving sensitivity for real regressions. It also adds a staged throttle rollout guard that gracefully applies backpressure during sustained degradation instead of immediate failover.

What this changes (high level):
- perf-canary/orchestrator: new TrafficCurator component that stratifies live traffic into cohorts by request shape (seq_len buckets), origin, and synthetic probe budget. It exposes a lightweight API used by the probe scheduler to decide which traffic to sample for canary comparisons.
- perf-canary/probes: probe-scaling configuration (probe_credit_budget, burst_resilience, temporal_strata) and logic for adaptive probe placement across replicas. Probes now use reservoir sampling with per-cohort weights so low-volume but important slices still get coverage.
- perf-canary/guards: StagedThrottleGuard implements a three-stage response to detected throughput/latency deltas: 1) soft-attenuation (reduce new canary traffic by fraction), 2) adaptive backpressure (increase probe density + throttle non-critical background routes), 3) circuit-escrow (hold critical traffic on safe model variant while rollouts pause). Each stage has configurable thresholds and cooldown windows.
- metrics/tracing: additional tags emitted for curator decisions (cohort, reason, probe_id) and guard decisions (stage, anchor_metric, confidence). These feed into console dashboards and the canary-runbook.
- tests: unit + integration harness: synthetic microburst generator, cohort replay tests, and a new e2e canary scenario that simulates slow memory-pressure-induced tail latency plus throughput drop.

Implementation notes:
- Baselines are estimated via an online quantile sketch per cohort (T-Digest variant) to keep memory bounded for high cardinality slices. The curator periodically compacts sketches and computes delta z-scores used by the guard.
- Probe scaling respects a global probe_credit_budget. Credits accrue on a per-window basis and are consumed by probes; when budget is low the curator prioritizes high-SLO cohorts using a priority function.
- StagedThrottleGuard uses a hysteresis-aware cooldown: each escalation stage has a soft deadline; if metrics recover within deadline the guard de-escalates without rollback.
- Safety: defaults are conservative to avoid customer-visible impact; the guard is opt-in per deployment until one week of canary metrics collection after rollout.

Related work: replaces ad-hoc heuristics from ENG-1920 and complements the rollout-sentinel in ENG-1805 by focusing on sample quality and controlled throttling rather than immediate cutoff.

Checklist:
- [x] Traffic curation algorithm and API
- [x] Probe scaling config + scheduler integration
- [x] StagedThrottleGuard implementation + unit tests
- [x] E2E harness scenario and CI jobs
- [x] Metrics/tags wired to console panels

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: misprioritization of cohorts could under-sample important traffic. Mitigation: default priority function favors low-volume auth/enterprise routes; manual overrides per-tenant are supported.
- Risk: sketch drift during traffic shifts. Mitigation: periodic full-window compaction and a fallback to rolling-window histograms when drift detected.

Rollout plan:
1) merge to main behind feature flag off
2) enable on perf-canary staging for two days, collect telemetry
3) smoke enable on 10% of canaries, monitor for false positives
4) full opt-in for all perf-canary runs after 7 days if stable

This PR is focused on production safety and reducing noisy rollbacks; it does not change model routing logic or model artifacts.

release_notes: Introduce traffic curation and staged throttle rollout guard for perf canaries; opt-in behind feature flag. Reduces false-positive rollbacks by improving probe sampling and adding a gradual backpressure policy.
